issue: Does the substantive-versus-clarifying test govern whether the Sentencing Commission's 2023 amendment to the compassionate-release Policy Statement (U.S.S.G. § 1B1.13) can apply to a sentence-reduction motion, so that an amendment treated as substantive cannot be applied to motions pending or filed before it took effect?

sides.position: The substantive-versus-clarifying test does not apply to sentence-modification proceedings, so the amended Policy Statement is not barred from applying to compassionate-release motions on that basis.
cases: United States v. Rutherford, 120 F.4th 360 (3d Cir. 2024)

sides.position: The amended Policy Statement is a substantive amendment that cannot be given retroactive effect to compassionate-release motions.
cases: United States v. Handlon, 97 F.4th 829, 833 (11th Cir. 2024)
United States v. Rutherford, 120 F.4th 360 (3d Cir. 2024)

this_court: The Third Circuit holds that the substantive-versus-clarifying test does not apply to a sentence modification, and it declines to follow Handlon.
quote: We part ways here with the Eleventh Circuit. United States v. Handlon, 97 F.4th 829, 833 (11th Cir. 2024) (holding that the amended Policy Statement is a substantive amendment that cannot be given retroactive effect).
cite: United States v. Daniel Rutherford, 120 F.4th 360 (3rd Cir. 2024)
